source_text.body:
Sign up for races with a browser agent
RunSignup staff had Meta's Muse agent search events and fill in registration forms; it was harder than advertised, but the second signup worked using a saved password and virtual card.
·
Nov 19, 2026
Done with
MM
Meta Muse
What they did
RunSignup staff used Meta's Muse, which searched RunSignup, GiveSignup and TicketSignup events. It then opened a browser, read pages, filled in forms and clicked buttons. Staff granted Muse access through Facebook or Instagram, enabled Stripe Link for payment, and used test accounts rather than real ones. Muse asked for approval before paying.
How it went
The first signup was clunky, with repeated chat questions about shirt size and address. On the second race Muse remembered the login and details, so it only asked which event and for waiver agreement. It doesn't support Apple Pay.
Worth knowing
You must trust the agent with your RunSignup password and a payment method, and Muse needs Stripe Link enabled. The team used non-real accounts for the test.
Try it yourself
with
Meta Muse
Copy prompt
Find [number] upcoming [5K/10K/half marathon/other] races within [distance] of [city] between [start date] and [end date], and list name, date, price, and registration link. Then open the registration page for [chosen race] and fill in my details: [name, birthdate, email, shirt size]. Stop before entering payment or submitting, and show me exactly what's filled in so I can approve it.
Original source: https://info.runsignup.com/2026/09/27/signing-up-for-races-with-metas-muse-ai-agent/
